Article Title: 'Avoid airing anti-national content': Govt warns TV channels against inflammatory debates and AI misuse
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of information and broadcasting on Wednesday issued an advisory to satellite TV channels, asking them to avoid live coverage of anti-terror operations, exercise caution while broadcasting violent visuals and refrain from airing anti-national content.In its advisory, the ministry asked channels to strictly adhere to the Programme Code prescribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, and the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994."The ministry of information & broadcasting has observed instances of non-compliance with the provisions of the Programme Code prescribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, and the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, by various private satellite television channels," the ministry said."Instances of similar news/visuals broadcast on multiple channels on similar topics were observed during the meeting of IDC. Therefore, IDC recommended that all private satellite television channels be advised to strictly adhere to the statutory provisions governing content broadcast on television. The committee also emphasised that inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalized in telecast," it added.The guidelines cover live coverage of anti-terror operations, violent visuals, crime reporting, natural disasters, the use of authentic maps of India, communal harmony and the protection of sexual assault victims' identities.On communal harmony and debate programmes, the ministry said channels must ensure that programmes, including live debates and panel discussions, "do not promote or encourage communal or anti-national attitudes".Broadcasters have also been cautioned to exercise due care while using artificial intelligence, including generative AI, in programmes such as graphics and virtual news presentations.The ministry said AI tools "may be limited to assistive capacity" without compromising the "accuracy, authenticity, or sensitivity" of news content.The ministry further asked broadcasters to strengthen their editorial and content-review mechanisms and regularly sensitise and train personnel involved in news gathering, editing, production, transmission and telecast.The ministry said violations of these guidelines may invite action under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995.
Article Summary: The guidelines cover live coverage of anti-terror operations, violent visuals, crime reporting, natural disasters, communal harmony and the protection of sexual assault victims' identities. Broadcasters have also been cautioned to exercise due care while using artificial intelligence, including generative AI, in programmes such as graphics and virtual news presentations.

Article Title: Anthropic introduces Claude Duet AI agent app for professionals: Features, availability and more
Article Text:
Anthropic introduces Claude Duet AI agent app for professional

Claude Duet: What can the new AI agent do

Claude Duet supports thousands of business tools

Claude Duet availability and subscription details

Anthropic has introduced Claude Duet, a new AI-powered app designed to help professionals and small business owners manage their work with less manual effort. The app can monitor connected accounts, flag tasks that need attention, prepare reports and handle work in the background, even when users step away from their devices. Unlike a chatbot that waits for instructions, Claude Duet can proactively alert users about important updates and help complete tasks across different apps. The research preview is now open through a waitlist for users in the US with Claude Pro and Max subscriptions, with access available on iOS, Android and the web.“We built Claude Duet for professionals and small business owners with more on their plates than they can track,” Anthropic said.According to the company, Claude Duet is designed to help users manage busy schedules and prioritise important work. Each morning, it can send a short summary of key items across connected apps. It then checks those accounts every few hours and sends notifications when something needs attention.Users can also assign tasks, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting emails to building dashboards, preparing financial forecasts and developing web apps.The app is built around Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 model and is designed to decide which tasks need immediate attention and when it should ask users for guidance.One of the key features of Claude Duet is its ability to continue working when users are away from their phones or computers. The app uses a virtual machine with its own browser to carry out tasks in the background. Users can send instructions through text or voice in a single ongoing conversation and receive a notification when a task is complete or requires their review.Claude Duet also carries over existing memory, skills and connected apps from a user's Claude account, which Anthropic says should make setup easier.Anthropic says Claude Duet is designed to ask for permission before taking important actions on a user's behalf. The app can read messages, draft replies and prepare work independently. However, it must seek approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting anything.Some actions, such as trading securities or transferring money between accounts, are not allowed even with user approval.The company has also introduced additional safeguards to protect sensitive information. According to Anthropic, the system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive details, such as credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, including health and personal financial details, can be shared only when users have explicitly instructed the app to do so.Claude Duet can connect with more than 6,000 connectors and plugins through the Claude Marketplace, allowing it to work with tools used by businesses. These integrations can help users find missed messages in Gmail and Slack, track unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe, prepare payroll in Gusto, draft job postings for LinkedIn and manage customer information in HubSpot.It can also help businesses create marketing campaigns using Canva and manage Shopify stores. Anthropic says support for a richer visual editor for Shopify storefronts is coming soon.Users can also make business purchases through Link, Stripe's digital wallet, and use Shop Pay for online checkout. Support for signing in to websites through saved 1Password logins is planned for a future update.Anthropic has opened a research preview of Claude Duet through a waitlist, starting with Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US. The app is available as a standalone offering on iOS and Android, as well as through claude.ai.During the preview, Claude Duet shares the same usage limits as the user's existing Claude plan. Background checks and complex tasks can consume those limits more quickly than ordinary conversations.
Article Summary: Claude Duet is designed to help professionals and small business owners manage their work with less manual effort. The app can monitor connected accounts, flag tasks that need attention, prepare reports and handle work in the background. Unlike a chatbot that waits for instructions, Claude Duet can proactively alert users about important updates and help complete tasks.

Article Title: Angry protestors 'interrupt' Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's event in Berlin, shout: 'What about technology found in Russian drones, those were ...'
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Nvidia CEO on 'Berlin protests'

Nvidia chips 'found' in Russian drones

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote address at the company’s GTC conference in Berlin was interrupted by protestors on Wednesday morning. Minutes into the keynote, hecklers stood on chairs in the auditorium displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" While the disruption was largely missed by the official livestream, attendee footage posted to Twitter captured demonstrators pressing Huang directly."Jensen, what about the technology that was found in Russian drones? Those were Nvidia chips. What are you doing about that?" one demonstrator shouted across the hall. "What are you doing about that? What are you doing about the environmental destruction?" The demonstration occurred during Nvidia’s three-day GTC Berlin event, running from October 20–22, which features developer sessions, executive panels, and industry talks alongside Huang’s opening address.The Nvidia CEO too made a small mention of the protests on stage, jokingly, he said, "All important issues, but let me get through my keynote." Huang remarked this before resuming the presentation.The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components—specifically within Russia's S-71 "Monochrome" weapon, which relies on consumer-grade Jetson Orin modules for autonomous targeting—as well as in cruise missiles deployed against Ukraine.Some reports in August identified an autonomous Russian AI drone powered by Jetson Orin hardware as the cause of three civilian deaths in Ukraine, marking the first documented case of its kind.A Russian Molniya drone allegedly carrying an Nvidia Jetson Orin module crashed and killed three civilians at a gas station in Zaporizhzhia in August after choosing its final target without a human pilot. A New York Times investigation cited Ukrainian air defense commanders, drone experts, and the forensic team that examined the wreckage, as source of their report.Nvidia confirmed to the New York Times that modules photographed in the recovered drones were Jetson Orin minicomputers, hardware that sells for a few hundred dollars. "Our Jetson Orin modules are consumer-grade products sold to students, developers, and startups for a wide range of beneficial applications," an Nvidia spokesperson reportedly told Tom's Hardware.The statement added, "They are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes. Pre-owned Jetsons are available through many reseller channels. Although we cannot track products after they are sold, if we determine that any customer is violating U.S. export controls, we will take appropriate action."
Article Summary: Protestors interrupted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's keynote address at GTC conference in Berlin. Demonstrators stood on chairs displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "N Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components in Russian drones and cruise missiles.

Article Title: PHP2Shell: Governments on high alert over critical website flaw; Wikipedia, hospitals, school portals go dark; what users should know
Article Text:
PHP2Shell: AI finds decade-old flaw in software behind 70% of websites; governments take sites offline

PHP is the hidden software behind most websites on the internet

The PHP2Shell flaw lets hackers take over a website without a password

AI found a flaw that had been hiding for over a decade

Most users on the internet can relax, but website owners need to update right away

A large chunk of the internet went offline on Wednesday, and most of it was switched off on purpose. Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down after two serious security flaws were found in PHP. Most people have never heard of PHP, but it is the software running behind roughly 70% of all websites, from news sites and online shops to personal blogs.The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them. PHP's developers released a fix on October 21, but hackers moved within hours to attack websites that hadn't updated yet. Cyber security agencies in the US and the UK have told website owners to install the fix right away or take their sites offline until they can.The list of affected sites shows how far PHP reaches. The Dutch government's own cyber security agency shut its website as a precaution. Finland took several government online services offline, France's Interior Ministry put all its websites into maintenance mode, and Denmark shut its national school communication platform.In the Netherlands, the Port of Rotterdam, the national football association, several hospitals and the five largest political parties also took their sites down. The Internet Archive went offline briefly, and online forums 4chan and DeviantArt ran into trouble. Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline.Some world leaders got involved too. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on X: "We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight."The rush makes sense once you see how fast hackers moved. Cloudflare, a company that sits in front of millions of websites to protect them, saw thousands of hacking attempts even before the flaws were made public. CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X that this climbed to tens of thousands within 45 minutes of the announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions by the next morning.Think of a website as having two sides. The side you see is the page in your browser. The side you don't see is a computer, called a server, that builds that page every time you open it. It fetches the right text, images, prices or comments from a database and sends the finished page to your screen. PHP is the language that does this job for a huge share of the web.It has been around since the early 1990s, and it powers WordPress, the tool behind millions of blogs and business websites. It also runs Wikipedia, many government portals, and platforms like Drupal and Joomla that big organisations use to manage their websites. Web tracking firm W3Techs estimates PHP is used by about 69.3% of all websites whose underlying software it can identify.That is why a single flaw in PHP turned into a global problem. Tiffany Farriss, who heads the Drupal Association, told Reuters that any server running a version of PHP from the last 20 years would be vulnerable. "This issue impacts the majority of the internet," she said.PHP is also free and open source, which means anyone can use it. It is looked after by a small non-profit, the PHP Foundation, which has just 13 full-time and part-time engineers maintaining software that much of the internet depends on.Normally, to change a website or access its stored data, you need an administrator login. PHP2Shell skips that step entirely.The two flaws, officially tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity. In simple terms, a hacker can send a website a carefully crafted request that makes PHP run out of memory and stop halfway through its work. That leaves behind some leftover data in the server. The hacker then sends a second request that makes PHP use that leftover data as if it were normal, and that opens the door to running their own commands on the server.Once inside, a hacker can change what a website shows, plant malicious software that infects visitors, or steal what the server stores. That can include usernames and passwords, digital keys that connect the site to other services, and databases with personal information. A second route even lets hackers peek into the server's short-term memory, where they could catch passwords and login details of other people using the site at the same time.Wiz, one of the firms that found the flaws, showed working attacks on fresh WordPress, Drupal and Joomla websites. It also pointed out that the problem is in PHP itself, so even a basic website with nothing complicated on it can be at risk. Every version of PHP going back more than a decade is affected.The bugs were found by two security firms working separately. Calif says it spotted them on August 1 with the help of an AI model, which OpenAI says was its GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz found them on August 19 using its own AI tool along with Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol.What stands out is that the flaws were not new. PHP's own developers had considered a possible attack along these lines in 2024, but nobody could work out how to make it happen. According to Wiz, turning these bugs into a real attack required so many complex steps that it was at the edge of what human experts could manage. With AI, a single researcher did in a week what would earlier have taken a top team months.The plan was to keep the flaws secret until October 22, giving website companies time to prepare fixes quietly. That plan fell apart when details leaked on online forums and social media on Tuesday. PHP rushed its fix out nearly a day early. Amazon later said its systems saw a hacking attempt on October 17, four days before the public announcement, and nobody yet knows how that attacker found out.OpenAI said in a blog post that the episode shows how AI can uncover security flaws, but also how it can help attackers "rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits." The same kind of AI that found the bug can help hackers study the fix and build an attack in very little time. That is why the window between a fix coming out and attacks starting has shrunk from days to minutes.If you only browse the web, there isn't much you need to do. The flaw targets the servers that run websites, not your phone or laptop. Still, a hacked website can be used to spread malware or steal data, so stay alert for a few weeks. If a service you use asks you to change your password, do it through the official app or website. Be careful with emails or messages about the PHP flaw that ask you to click links or share details, as scammers often use big news like this as bait.If you run a website, even a small blog, check whether it uses PHP. Sites built on Squarespace or Wix are safe, as those platforms don't use PHP. Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, says websites it hosts directly, along with Tumblr, are safe. If you installed WordPress yourself or use a hosting company like GoDaddy, Bluehost or Hostinger, contact your provider to find out when the fix will reach your site.The fixed versions of PHP are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Websites running PHP 8.1 or older won't get a fix at all, because those versions are no longer supported, so they need to move to a newer version. If your site stores customer details or takes payments and you can't confirm it has been fixed, taking it offline for a few hours is the safer choice. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has also asked organisations that couldn't update quickly to check whether hackers have already left a hidden way back into their systems.Small websites run by individuals and small businesses are the most at risk, since they often lack a technical team and depend on their hosting company to apply fixes.Sigi Goode, a professor of information systems at the Australian National University, told The Guardian where the real danger lies. "The bigger concern is the websites that are not down today," he said. The websites that went dark on Wednesday were the ones taking the threat seriously. The ones still online without the fix are what hackers will be hunting for in the weeks ahead.
Article Summary: Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down. The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them.

Article Title: Two Swiss brothers spent about £10,000 turning a 15-by-15-metre section of their garden into a miniature Greek village with blue shutters, stone lanes and a bar; the wider backyard attraction cost £20
Article Text:
Scherrer and his brother have transformed 600 square metres of their expansive 1,500-square-metre garden into themed attractions.

A Greek escape at home

From garden to theme park

A backdrop for unexpected holidays

The next chapter

For most people, a summer escape means booking a flight, packing a suitcase and leaving home behind. For Michael Scherrer, the holiday destination is considerably closer. In his garden in Switzerland, the 48-year-old content creator has spent a year transforming a modest patch of land into a miniature Greek village, complete with cobbled lanes, blue shutters and a traditional-style bar. Built with the help of his brother Samuel, 46, the project turns the idea of a backyard makeover into something closer to a private theme park. Scroll down to read the details.According to a Daily Mail report, the Greek village occupies a 15-by-15-metre section of the garden and cost around £10,000 to create. Its design is intended to evoke the character of a Mediterranean holiday, with winding stone pathways, tiny buildings, vivid blue details and carefully designed spaces that encourage visitors to linger.At the centre of the experience is a small bar, positioned so that guests can sit surrounded by the village rather than simply looking at it from the outside. The effect is deliberately immersive, creating the sensation of stepping into another country without leaving the property, adds the online report.On the other hand, PEOPLE reported that Scherrer built the village as a place where he and his clients could sit and talk, but the project quickly became much more ambitious.Planning permissions and unpredictable weather in Switzerland extended the construction process, turning what began as a gardening and building project into a substantial long-term undertaking.The Greek village is only one part of a much larger attraction. Scherrer and his brother have around 1,500 square metres available for their creative projects and have so far developed approximately 600 square metres.The wider garden has already taken on the character of a miniature theme park, with spaces inspired by different countries, ideas and seasons. Alongside the Greek setting is a Japanese garden, while an Irish bar and Halloween-themed areas add contrasting moods to the landscape, adds the Daily Mail report.The project has cost approximately £20,000 overall, with each section designed to offer a different visual experience. Rather than following one consistent aesthetic, the brothers have embraced the garden as a constantly evolving collection of themed environments, adds the report.The miniature village has also become an unlikely social-media prop. Its convincing details have allowed friends and family to take photographs that appear, at first glance, to have been taken abroad.The Daily Mail reported on the unusual backyard transformation, highlighting how visitors have used the setting to fool friends and colleagues into believing they have actually travelled to Greece. The illusion works precisely because of the attention paid to details such as the architecture, colour palette and layout of the tiny village.For Scherrer, however, the appeal goes beyond photographs. The garden provides a physical escape during the summer, creating a space where ordinary evenings can take on the atmosphere of a Mediterranean getaway.As per PEOPLE, the village is not necessarily finished. Scherrer has considered turning one of the tiny homes into a guest room, potentially adding a bed during spring so visitors could stay within the miniature setting.There are also plans for new themed areas, including a fishing village and another room for guests. The garden is still evolving, with a pirate ship among the possibilities.Small world gardens that tell stories and grow plants are popular. What began with two brothers wanting to garden and build has evolved into an imaginative landscape where Greece, Japan, Ireland and seasonal fantasy can coexist within a single Swiss backyard.Images Courtesy: Instagram/smallest_themepark
Article Summary: Michael Scherrer and his brother have transformed 600 square metres of their expansive 1,500-square-metre garden into themed attractions. The project has cost approximately £20,000 overall, with each section designed to offer a different visual experience. The garden is still evolving, with a pirate ship among the possibilities.

Article Title: An Australian designer develops hempcrete tiles to recreate tree hollows and rocky crevices; shelters aim to help threatened wildlife, including eastern quolls and ringtail possums
Article Text:
How hempcrete tiles recreate tree hollows and rocky crevices

Why Australia's wildlife needs alternative shelters

Which animals could benefit from Bush Cradle?

Eastern quolls

Ringtail possums

Other native wildlife

Early field observations offer an encouraging sign

Who developed Bush Cradle?

What comes next for the project?

Australian designer Xavier Earls has developed Bush Cradle, a modular wildlife habitat system made from hempcrete tiles that mimic natural shelters such as tree hollows, fallen logs and rocky crevices. The system is designed to help conservationists create customised refuges for native animals facing habitat loss. Its four interlocking tile designs can be assembled into different configurations, including tree hollows and ground dens, with entrances tailored to individual species. The project aims to address the shortage of natural shelter for wildlife, including eastern quolls and ringtail possums. In an encouraging early observation, ringtail possums reportedly used a prototype overnight, offering an initial indication of the design's potential.Bush Cradle uses four tile shapes connected through a slot-and-pin mechanism, allowing shelters to be assembled, dismantled and rearranged by hand without conventional tools. This makes it possible to adapt their configurations to different species and environments.The tiles are made from fibrous hempcrete, chosen for its insulating properties. Their manufacture combines 3D printing and casting, with lightweight printed frames placed inside moulds before hempcrete is poured in and left to cure.Laser-cut wooden entrance pieces allow openings to be customised for different animals.According to Earls' project description, the developed tiles weigh approximately 200 grams each, compared with early prototypes that weighed more than one kilogram. The modular design also allows individual components to be repaired or replaced without discarding an entire shelter.Natural features such as tree hollows, fallen logs and rocky crevices provide essential places for animals to rest, nest, hide from predators and raise their young. However, land clearing, development and habitat degradation are reducing the availability of these refuges.Tree hollows are particularly important for many native species, but they can take hundreds of years to form naturally. When mature trees disappear, the animals that depend on their hollows can lose essential shelter long before replacement habitats develop.Bush Cradle offers a potential way to bridge this gap by allowing conservationists to construct artificial refuges suited to particular species and landscapes. Its adaptable components provide an alternative to conventional nest boxes, which are often designed for a specific purpose.The system is intended to accommodate different native Australian animals by allowing shelters to be tailored to their habitat requirements.: These spotted, nocturnal marsupials use dens and other sheltered spaces. Bush Cradle can be configured to mimic hollow logs and ground refuges, with entrances and chambers adapted to their needs.: These tree-dwelling marsupials need protected places to rest. A Bush Cradle prototype installed in a tree was reportedly occupied by wild ringtail possums overnight.: Earls has identified potential applications for pygmy possums, reptiles, endangered skinks and microbats. Different configurations could accommodate their varying entrance sizes and shelter requirements.Trail-camera footage reportedly recorded ringtail possums using a Bush Cradle prototype installed in a tree overnight. The observation provided an early indication that the structure could serve as a usable refuge beyond the design studio.However, a single observation cannot establish whether the shelters improve long-term survival, breeding success or population recovery. Further monitoring would be needed to determine how consistently different species use the structures and how well they perform under varying weather conditions.Earls created Bush Cradle as his final-year industrial design project at Monash University in Australia. His work combines ecological research, digital modelling, 3D printing and material experimentation to explore how design could help address habitat loss.An internship at Reef Design Lab helped him explore how digital fabrication and casting could be combined to produce habitat structures. Earls now works full-time at the organisation, continuing to investigate how design can support ecosystems.Bush Cradle received a Best in Class Award in the Next Gen category at the 2026 Australian Good Design Awards, according to Monash University. The recognition highlighted the project's approach to combining industrial design with wildlife conservation.Earls aims to establish a network of conservationists who can use Bush Cradle to create customised wildlife refuges in Australia and potentially elsewhere. The project has also attracted interest for possible use in restoring habitat for endangered skinks and microbats in mining-affected areas of northern Queensland.The long-term ambition is to make artificial habitat creation more accessible, allowing conservationists to respond to the requirements of different species rather than relying on a single shelter design.
Article Summary: Australian designer Xavier Earls has developed a modular wildlife habitat system made from hempcrete tiles. The system is designed to help conservationists create customised refuges for native animals facing habitat loss. Its four interlocking tile designs can be assembled into different configurations, including tree hollows and ground dens, with entrances tailored to individual species.

Article Title: A Buckinghamshire wildlife garden redesigned around an unheated natural swimming pond that attracts frogs, bats, and dragonflies
Article Text:
Image: Julie Skelton

A wildlife and wellbeing brief, how Rachel Platt connected a Buckinghamshire garden to the countryside

Inside the unheated natural swimming pool, a plant-free swim zone and a planted regeneration zone

Frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds, all the wildlife that has moved into the garden's ponds

The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value (Image: Julie Skelton)

How drainage reshaped the plan and kept old favourites

Edible hedgerow, uncut winter meadow, and autumn colour; planting that completes the wildlife garden

A place where the daily swim could begin at the back door, surrounded by dragonflies and flowering plants, even in winter, was the dream of two owners in south Buckinghamshire, who work in the veterinary sector and wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt answered with an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, bats, dragonflies, and more. Read on to discover how the design works, which plants and features support wildlife, what changed along the way, and how the owners describe their transformed outdoor sanctuary. The garden shows how thoughtful landscaping can combine everyday enjoyment with a thriving habitat, creating a peaceful retreat that evolves with the seasons.According to Homes and Gardens, which featured the project in an article by Rachel Bull, the owners both work in the veterinary sector and dreamed of a garden linked to the rolling fields and hedgerows around them. Their brief asked for a biodiverse landscape that would support wildlife while also providing space to swim, grow food, entertain, and spend more time outdoors. Rachel Platt Garden Design responded with a layout that deliberately changes character as it moves away from the house: stronger geometry near the building gives way to softer curves, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an experimental edible hedgerow toward the fields beyond.Before the redesign, the owners regularly drove elsewhere to swim in rivers and spent relatively little time in their own garden, so the new design was meant to bring that experience home.At the heart of the garden sits an unheated natural swimming pool, created as both a wildlife habitat and a place for the owners to reconnect with nature, Homes and Gardens reports. Designer Rachel Platt developed it in collaboration with Ellicar Natural Pools. The pool is divided into a swim zone, kept clear of plants and wildlife, and a regeneration zone planted with a range of aquatic species that filter the water naturally, a process the article calls hydrobotanical filtration. Around the shoreline, water mint, water forget-me-nots, native flag irises, marsh marigolds, ragged robin, and purple loosestrife add colour, seasonal structure, and fragrance, flowering from March to September and attracting pollinators and moths. Deeper-growing aquatics such as common water plantain and arrowhead offer late summer flowers and seedheads, and give emerging dragonflies stems to climb while they unfurl their wings.The wildlife has arrived in force. Homes and Gardens reports that dragonflies and bats were already drawn to the pool, with planting softening its edges and tying it into the wider ecosystem. The owners told Homes and Gardens that frogs, toads, and newts breed in all the ponds, as do several dragonfly species, and that they have even spotted a water snake. Birds also visit, using a beach area, a feature not found in conventional ponds, to enter the water and bathe safely. The owners described the pond as a total escape through every season, and said the garden has become a haven where they feel miles away from everything. For anyone planning a wildlife garden, the lesson is that a single well-planned water feature can support amphibians, insects, mammals, and birds at the same time.The pool was not always meant to be round. According to Homes and Gardens, the original concept was a formal linear pond positioned to reflect a mature birch tree visible through large French doors off the open-plan kitchen and living space. Existing drainage and a suspected utility service running across the garden forced a rethink, and the design became a circular pool. Sustainability and sentiment guided other decisions too. The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value and the wildlife they support, and much of the existing planting was saved or relocated, including the owners' fig tree, lily of the valley, raspberries, and rhubarb. Reusing what already works reduces waste and preserves habitat, while keeping familiar plants gives the new garden a sense of continuity with the owners' past.Beyond the pool, an edible hedge links the garden to the landscape, Homes and Gardens says, combining common hazel, hawthorn, blackberry, black chokeberry, damson, pear, and serviceberry to provide structure, blossom, fruit, and habitat. It leads gradually into the meadow, which the owners deliberately leave uncut over winter so that insects, birds, and small mammals can feed on seeds and find a place to overwinter. Autumn colour was also requested, so ornamental grasses such as Miscanthus 'Beth Chatto' and perennials such as Ceratostigma plumbaginoides and white gaura carry warm tones, while burning bush adds bright red. A kitchen garden, grapevine pergola, firepit, and outdoor shower complete the picture. Summing up the transformation, the owners told Homes and Gardens, "We really have our own little Eden," and called the redesign the best decision they have ever made.
Article Summary: Two owners in Buckinghamshire wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt designed an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds.

Article Title: Oura Ring 5 launches in India, price starts at Rs 39,900
Article Text:
Oura Ring 5 features

Oura Ring 5 price in India

Silver and Black: Rs 39,900

Gold, Deep Rose, Stealth and Brushed Silver: Rs 50,900

Oura has launched its latest generation smart ring in India – Oura Ring. Said to be 40 percent smaller than Oura Ring 4, Oura Ring 5 features a more compact and comfortable design, with next-generation sensing, advanced health insights and up to one week of battery life. The all-new Oura Ring pre-orders begin starting October 22 in the country through Amazon and Croma.George Abbott, Head of EMEA and APAC at Oura said: “India represents an exciting opportunity for Oura as more people look to technology that fits seamlessly into their lives, helping them not just track their health, but better understand it through increasingly personalised and predictive insights. Oura Ring 5 brings that vision to life: it’s smaller and more comfortable to wear, including during exercise and sport, while giving members a deeper understanding of how their sleep, activity, stress and recovery connect. We’re excited to bring that experience to more people across India.”As mentioned above, the Oura Ring 5 is 40% smaller than its predecessor, Ring 4. Its next-generation sensing architecture combines more powerful LEDs with 12 optimised signal pathways to capture clearer, more reliable health signals across a wider range of finger types and skin tones. These signals are translated through the Oura App into personalised, actionable insights across health, activity and wellbeing.The smart ring is claimed to have 6-9 days of battery life on a single charge - depending on size and usage. Its will be available in sizes 6 to 13 and six finishes, including Black, Silver, Stealth, Brushed Silver, a redesigned Gold in a lighter, modern shade closer to true gold, and Deep Rose in a rich copper-rose finish.For members in India, Oura Ring 5 pairs its re-engineered sensing with Oura’s latest health experiences. Building on Symptom Radar, which launched in 2024, Health Radar continuously monitors key biometric signals in the background to help members identify meaningful changes and patterns that may warrant attention. At the heart of Health Radar is Blood Pressure Signals, which analyses 30 days of nighttime ring data to help members identify patterns that may indicate cardiovascular strain. Alongside it, Nighttime BP uses overnight PPG signals to surface blood-pressure-related patterns and longer-term trends, offering insights into cardiovascular health that may not be apparent from daytime measurements alone.Members can also log readings from a blood pressure cuff directly in the Oura App, keeping these measurements alongside their broader health data. Blood Pressure Signals and Nighttime BP are wellness features: they don’t measure blood pressure in mmHg or diagnose any condition. Health Radar also includes Nighttime Breathing, providing a rolling 30-day view of sleep-related breathing patterns and disturbances. By looking beyond individual nights, the sleep wellness experience helps members recognise changes over time and better understand when further evaluation by a healthcare professional may be warranted.Oura Ring 5 will also offer GLP-1 Insights that brings medication tracking and continuous biometric data together in one place. GLP-1 Insights is available in India through the Oura App in English for members with Oura Ring Gen3 or newer. Other features include Oura’s Menopause Insights, Cardio Effort and automatic VO2 Max.Starting October 22nd, 2026, Oura Ring 5 will be available for pre-order in all Croma stores in India, as well as online through Amazon. Oura Ring 5 is priced at -Oura membership, on the other hand, will cost Rs 599 per month.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Microsoft expands sovereign cloud tools to give businesses greater control over data and AI
Article Text:
Here’s the full blog post shared by Microsoft’s Douglas Phillips

Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates expand its Microsoft Sovereign Cloud offering, allowing organisations to choose how and where sensitive data and applications are managed, including in environments that can operate without an internet connection. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally. Microsoft said the move is designed to help organisations meet regional regulations, strengthen security and keep critical services running during disruptions, while continuing to use cloud and AI technology."This challenge is becoming more important as advanced cloud and AI capabilities move into public services, regulated processes and essential operations. Organizations are considering more than where data resides. They also seek to understand who can access and operate their systems, how sensitive digital assets remain protected, which technology dependencies matter most and whether critical services can continue as regulatory, geopolitical, security or network conditions change.Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate.Last year, we introduced Microsoft Sovereign Cloud to give customers more choice in how they address these requirements. Since then, we have continued to turn our commitments into practical capabilities across public cloud and customer-operated environments, while expanding how we enable partners to address sovereignty requirements in their local markets. Today, we are sharing the next stage of that work.A continuum of control, built around the workloadMicrosoft Sovereign Cloud diagram showing a continuum of sovereignty solutions across three areas: Sovereign Public Cloud for control, data protection and regional requirements; Sovereign Private Cloud for critical workloads across connected and disconnected environments; and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem for trusted, locally operated and specialized solutions.Our approach to digital sovereignty starts with the workload. Each workload carries different requirements for data, operations, technology dependencies, continuity and risk. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed to make it easier for organizations to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload without forcing every application into the same deployment model.Those needs can vary widely across organizations. A public-facing digital service may benefit from the scale and pace of innovation in the public cloud. A system supporting essential operations may need to continue running locally if connectivity is disrupted. An AI workload handling highly sensitive data may require models, data and processing to remain within a customer-controlled environment.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed around this workload-based approach, providing a continuum of management, control and options across Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem. Organizations can apply the level of control appropriate to each workload while maintaining a consistent approach to governance and operations across their digital estate. Sovereign Public Cloud adds capabilities for workloads that require greater control and transparency while continuing to benefit from the scale and innovation of Azure.Sovereign Private Cloud extends cloud capabilities into customer-operated environments, including connected and disconnected operations. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the continuum through independently operated environments, specialized partners, locally relevant expertise and technologies that support customers’ sovereignty requirements.These are not isolated destinations. Customers can combine public cloud, private cloud and partner capabilities across their digital estate, applying different levels of control to different workloads as their operating needs evolve.Making control more visible in Sovereign Public CloudFor many workloads, the public cloud provides a combination of scale, innovation, integrated security and compliance. Organizations can benefit from these capabilities while applying additional sovereignty controls for residency, confidentiality, operator access, policy and continuity. Our work in Sovereign Public Cloud makes these controls easier to understand, apply and demonstrate.Sovereign Control Panel, entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required.This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian, which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger, also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed.Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure.Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information.Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements.Designing for resilience and operational independenceFor some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption.To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns. These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed.For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change.Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local controlOperational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment.Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments.GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control.The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local. At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local, available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers.Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run.Azure Local will support multitenancy, allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure.These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload.Extending the continuum through partnersGraphic titled "Sovereign Partner Ecosystem" with the subtitle "National clouds · Software · Services · Platform co-innovation," showing 32 partner logos: Accenture, AMD, Armada, Avanade, base-it, Bleu, Capgemini, Cirrus Data, CloudCasa by Catalogic, Cronos Groep, cTelecoms, DataON, Delos Cloud, Dell Technologies, F5, Felo, Fortinet, HPE, Inspark, Intel, Lenovo, Mattermost, Mistral, NVIDIA, Qualidev, Qumulo, RiverMeadow, Rubrik, Supermicro, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Veeam and WSO2.Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions.The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds, including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge.This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload.The next chapter of digital sovereigntyAI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation.We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require."
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally.

Article Title: Sam Altman’s OpenAI reports two AI agents weakened internal monitoring systems
Article Text:
Here’s what OpenAI said

What happened

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In an update, the company said that a GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to its security team. In another case, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, the company revealed. “In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them,” OpenAI said in the blog post.In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. However, OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.In the blog post, OpenAI wrote:“In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications.In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that it had not removed the monitor. In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them. We are strengthening our misalignment monitoring system in response, and are also assessing whether these cases reflect benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.”On October 3, a researcher asked a GPT-6.1 Sol coding agent to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. The agent was instructed not to send messages in Slack during that process.82 user messages later, the pipeline stopped after its monitor flagged a proposed validation repair and was unable to save the finding to the monitoring database because it lacked the required access. The user then asked for more information about the alarm and about what needed to be done.Initially, the agent interpreted the user’s earlier instruction (“don’t send any messages”) as a restriction on outreach, separate from any issues with the monitoring system.The main agent initially interpreted the earlier no-slack-message instruction as a restriction on outreach, separate from automatic monitoring. Its recorded reasoning concluded that running the pipeline should have normal monitoring notifications enabled.The agent then delegated the task of repairing the monitoring system to a subagent, with an explicit instruction to preserve monitoring and publish genuine results. As it started its task, the subagent then considered again whether the user’s “don’t send any messages” instruction should affect its repair. It recognized that turning off notifications would disable required alerts, and decided not to recommend that exchange.While the subagent decided not to turn on no_notify since doing so would be unsafe, the main agent later reconsidered, reasoning that writing a result to the database could cause the central monitoring notifier to send a message to the user. Its reasoning weighted the expected alerting policy against the user’s earlier instructions, and finally settled on suppressing notifications based on the user’s instruction not to send messages.Based on its judgment that the user’s instruction not to send messages applied to the misalignment monitoring system, the parent agent then directed the subagent to force notification suppression. A follow-up message specified that the suppression requirement covered both the request metadata and the stored result.The subagent then implemented those instructions: its patch emptied the lists of people set to receive monitoring reports, set no_notify to true, and recorded the reason as a user request not to send messages. It also made suppression a prerequisite for writing a review result.
Article Summary: GPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. But OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.
